title: Testard, Amyraut and Camero's followers: grace works by persuading the mind
source_text: LI. Nam Paulus Testardus, & Moses Amyraldus, aliique qui cum iis in gratiae negotio Cameronis Methodum & doctrinam sequuntur, efficaciam gratiae divinae, quae hominem ad Deum convertit, eique fidem in Christum ingenerat, & Dei amore cor illius accendit, in eo consistere docent, quod salutaris veritas in Evangelio proposita eo modo menti offeratur, & arcana virtute spiritus mens intus ita disponatur, ut homo firmissimam & efficacissimam veritatis illius persuasionem inde concipiat, statuatque nihil melius, & ad veram beatitudinem obtinendam conducibilius, quam ut quis Christo adhaereat, & Evangelio illius obsequatur. Unde fit ut voluntas, quae ex eorum hypothesi, necessario sequitur ductum & judicium intellectus practici, bonum illud salutare per Evangelium oblatum, & ab intellectu monstratum suscipiat, atque avide complectatur: & sic a rebus vanis & terrenis aversa tota convertatur ad Deum, qua in re consistit ejus innovatio & sanctificatio.
pass_a_gloss: LI. For Paulus Testardus, & Moses Amyraldus, and others who with them follow the Method & doctrine of Camero in the matter of grace, teach that the efficacy of divine grace, which converts man to God, and begets in him faith in Christ, & kindles his heart with the love of God, consists in this, that the saving truth set forth in the Gospel is offered to the mind in such a way, & the mind is inwardly so disposed by the secret power of the spirit, that man thence conceives a most firm & most efficacious persuasion of that truth, and determines that nothing is better, & more conducive to obtaining true blessedness, than that one cleave to Christ, & obey his Gospel. Whence it comes about that the will, which on their hypothesis necessarily follows the lead & judgment of the practical intellect, takes up that saving good offered through the Gospel, & shown by the intellect, and eagerly embraces it: & so, turned away from vain & earthly things, it is wholly converted to God, in which consists its renewal & sanctification.
pass_b_english: Thesis LI. Paulus Testardus, Moses Amyraldus and the others who follow Camero's method and teaching on grace hold that the efficacy of God's grace, which turns a person to God, plants faith in Christ in him and sets his heart on fire with love for God, works like this. The saving truth set out in the Gospel is presented to the mind in a certain way, and the Spirit's hidden power so shapes the mind from within that the person comes to be utterly and effectively convinced of that truth.

He concludes that nothing is better, and nothing does more to bring a person to true happiness, than holding fast to Christ and obeying his Gospel. On their premise the will must follow where the practical intellect leads and what it judges, so the will takes up the saving good that the Gospel offers and the intellect points out, and grasps it eagerly. Turned away from empty and earthly things, it turns wholly to God, and in this its renewal and sanctification consist.
